payload.output:
Conditionally reading the supplied issuer table, a one-for-ten stock dividend adds one share for every ten held: the share-count multiplier is 1 + 1/10 = 1.1 (cib-dividends). An eligible hypothetical 1,000-share holding would receive 100 additional shares and become 1,100 shares, with no fractional issue in this fixture (scenario-bonus). The table labels this a stock dividend, not a split. A stock dividend distributes additional shares; a split subdivides existing shares under its own terms. Both can require per-share-price/history adjustments, but they are not interchangeable corporate-action descriptions.

There is a timing defect in the packet: cib-dividends has an actual capture timestamp of 2026-10-25T22:56:12.986Z, which is 17.761 seconds after this case's cutoff of 22:55:55.225Z. Thus the numerical extraction is explicitly conditional interpretation of the supplied text, not proof that this evidence was available at the strict cutoff. A new earlier verified source or a prospectively changed cutoff would be needed for an admissible as-of claim.

The table gives record and payment dates of 16 and 17 December 2025, respectively; it provides no ex-date. More shares alone do not establish an economic gain, bank earnings growth or stronger capital. Per-share prices may adjust, but no price path or adjustment vintage is supplied, so neither a raw-price change nor shareholder return can be calculated. Missing data include eligibility verification beyond the fixture, adjusted/unadjusted prices, other distributions, fees/taxes and action details. Bounded decision: retain the conditional 1,100-share scenario arithmetic, flag the cutoff issue, and withhold return and trade-clearance conclusions.
